tips.comment: Try Storm Cat has a great chance to make all the running here. Two solid runs so far and looks to be going in the right direct based on form. Not going to get rich on this but third time lucky today i am thinking for Try Storm Cat.

Dandy style is the Brother to two winning sprinters and wasn't beaten by much on his debut over 5f even after a bad stalls exit. Experience could've been good for him and just what he needed to get amongst it at the end here.

This Invincible Army gelding is an exciting contender. He is closely related to the 9f winner Rustikal and has 3 half-siblings who have won, including the notable 2-year-old 5f winner Fearless Angel and the mile and half winner Dark Oak. With Tim Easterby's expertise, a small each-way wager at 50/1 is definitely worth considering.
Lima Sierra has a good win under the belt last time and there is scope for me today as only a small raise in the weights. A lot of horse and not a lot of wins so Lima can make all and win this.

Baby Rover has taken a while to start competing but theres been more good runs than bad of late with 3 defeats coming by margins of 2 lenghts in the last 4 runs. Races off minimum weight and should be landing a place at minumum in a weak race

Glimmer Of Light is today’s standout bet at Redcar. Consistent recent form, strong trainer-jockey combo, and well-handicapped make it a compelling win candidate. Market confidence supports its chances, and it looks primed to strike in this Class 6 contest.

Went fourth inside the final furlong on soft ground at Carlisle just 5 days ago in a Class 5. Turned round quickly for this, remains on the same mark but drops to Class 6 and should welcome this quicker ground.
Ran on inside the final furlong when runner-up over a furlong further here last month and interesting dropping back to the minimum trip.

Winner at Musselburgh on final start last season who has returned with very solid efforts at Beverley and Nottingham this spring before well beaten at Chelmsford last time. Very much of interest back on turf here though.

Reservardo has hit the frame on all starts so far picking up 1 win from 6 in the process. Only beaten a length by an inform and handy looking rival last time out. Gets ideal draw from stall 1 and the Crisfords stable is going well, looks worthy favourite.

Narrow defeat here on handicap debut to a horse that went to on to land a hat trick. Flopped next time out on all weather run but should bounce back with good to firm seemingly in favour, low stall draw and sitting low in the weights
4 times winner but last of them was in May 2023. Did finish 3rd of 9 on penultimate outing and a repeat of that form would give an each way chance

Barleybrown is a risky each way choice as most of its form is on the all weather. The form doesnt look great at the moment but this one has a 18% win rate better than the front 5 in the market. Lets go for an each way here and see what we get.
Currently out of form and just 2 wins from 44 runs not exactly encouraging but has placed in 50% of those runs so stats sometimes can be a bit misleading and it helps last 2 runs have been here.

This C Appleby trained colt must be going well at home as he was a well backed favourite for his racecourse debut over seven furlongs on good to firm ground at Haydock and he duly obliged when easily beating the Dr R Newland & J Insole treained Island Bear by five lengths so with P J Dobbs onboard he can follow up today

Debut here for Pacific avenue. Stablemate to the favourite wild desert. Trainer knows a thing or two with debutants. With wild desert winning on debut and also being half brother to shadow of light who went off strong favourite this week at ascot. Great chance.
No comment made

Bit of a punt here but, Tony Carroll doesn't send many horses to HQ and this 7yo Starspangledbanner gelding is now 3 pounds below his LWM, has a 7 pound claimer aboard and drops in class here. Surely worth a go at double figure odds.

Was superb winning debut run at Salisbury around the same time last year but things have not gone to plan since then and switch to handicaps LTO in debut handicap run did not change fortunes when 8 of 9 at Newbury back in April of this year. Dropped mark and drop down in class just might be the difference.

Tides of War runs in the 4.25 at Newmarket and looks well-handicapped, especially with a valuable 7lb claim from Taryn Langley. He’s in good form, finishing second last time out, and now drops slightly in class. Conditions suit, and he should be competitive over this trip.

Dark Rosa entered my notebook following her race over this trip at Windsor earlier this month. She was backed into favourite after opening up at 12-1 but had an awful position trapped on the rail but ran on well when in the clear.
The form of Bintjan's last race is looking pretty solid and this horse remains relatively unexposed off this make. Good chance to score here.

Rebels Romance has been travelling the world with wins in Cologne and Del mar and Doha but returned at York in the Boodles Yorkshire Cup and although it wasn't straight forward victory his class came through. Drops back in distance shouldn't be a problem and is the one they have to beat.

With Aiden O'Brien having bagged six winners at the meeting already going into Friday, it could be time for son Joseph to get in on the act. Easy winner of a G1 in Germany last August following his second in the Eclipse, he had little chance in the Arc with a medium pace & a less than inspired ride. He reappeared in February where he reportedly tied-up in a G2 in Riyadh over an extended 1m 2f & found the trip too sharp again in a G1 in Longchamp 55 days ago. Freshened up for this , over his optimum trip, what we have here I believe is a G1 horse running in a G2 race for which you can get 6/1

The 4yo has been racing at the highest level and should be happier in this company. In three of his last four races at the highest level he has posted three 120 RPR ratings, which is top level form, despite not winning. He can be a big player at this Group 2 level.
Unsuited by the slow pace last time but still shaped well under a penalty. Has strong form over this course and looks one more a strong player.
Palladium looks overlooked here has Ryan Moore is enlisted to ride this Gosden runner and will give it all his assistance ...won the Geeman Derby and was sold for a tidy sum..lively one to consider

Highly promising gelded son of Sea The Stars & Newton's Angel ( Dam's sire Dark Angel ) who was last seen at Chester 43 days ago where finishing 5th/6 not seen to best effect on the occasion as he looked in need of the outing after a 261 day break however he wasn't totally disgraced and strongly appeals as the type to do much better now as a 4yo and he arrives here in top nick and well prepared to tackle this assignment steps back up in trip racing over the 1 mile 3 furlong trip that most certainly being a good move by his top connections as Space Legend will really appreciate this step back up in trip and worth noting he finished a very promising clear of rest 2nd/14 in last year's King Edward VII Stakes at this meeting jockey James Doyle takes the ride on William Haggas's inmate and can give Space Legend a promising ride here at Ascot in race that should suit Space Legend's nature of going very well given the horses enrolled to run here bold showing is anticipated and he must enter calculations here

This horse has a very good record fresh 
Has been lightly raced and has performed well here in the past.
The stable are in form and a big run is anticipated.

BURDETT ROAD is a 110 rated flat turf horse three times a winner in this sphere and this multi-purpose operator looks interesting coming from a classy dual-purpose yard who do well under both codes. This is a highly competitive renewal year-on-year , but he does not look out of place lining up and he brings bundles of back-class including course winning form on quick ground.

Very capable on his day and would be a shoe in on best form last season when a close second to Los Angeles in the Irish Derby and a close up promoted third to Jan Breughal in the St Leger. In between those two runs was a few lengths behind Rebel's Romance in the King George here at Ascot. Disappointing since but would t have to find much to get involved and first time blinkers might eke that improvement out. Oisin Murphy back onboard and can't let this former 2yo Gp 1 winner go unbacked at this price.

Not been able to figure Ascot just yet this period but just maybe Bellum Justum might change that who has the ability to bounce back strongly from a poor run LTO at Epsom earlier this month and is helped by a drop down in class.
Epic Poet this year has had four runs in group company 3232 with the latest being in G2 and just missing out by a head behind Robel's Romance and worth another shot EW 4P

Treanmor is beautifully bred and was very impressive first time out over 6 furlongs at Newmarket. It is surprising he is as big as 13/8 which is presumably down to the fact that Charlie Appleby hasn't had a Royal Ascot for a few years but his horses have been running well in defeat this week and the extra furlong here is a bonus.

Moments of joy was impressive on debut in Ireland and looks sure to.improve with that run.
The form of the stables 2 year olds is impressive and this can be yet another winner for them.
Convincing win on debut and related to Holloway Boy, who was as precocious as they come. If backing up from the debut, should be in with a real chance here

Pushed the stoutly bred Italy pretty hard on debut, with the pair well clear of Ipanema Beach who had previously trailed home behind the evidently very smart Charles Darwin on debut. He perhaps got going a little too soon there in a bid to sneak away, and will get no such luxury here, but that could lead to his hand being played a little later with some obvious forward going horses to latch onto. Fairly well stamina laden, if he can go the pace I’d hope he’d be bang there late on. It looks a winnable Chesham, where for once the O’Brien hand looks slightly questionable, albeit it can be a tip in itself that she’s the only one they rely on. Treanmor was impressive on debut for Godolphin, but his form there is questionable with 2nd places Vlad finishing behind a horse who was behind in the Windsor Castle, and a number of other horses in behind being sent packing since. A £2m purchase, he has to respected on that alone, but is short enough with that sort of form.
Won well on debut over six furlongs, getting well on top in the closing stages. This step up in trip could suit base on pedigree and is open to further improvement. Good chance.
Despite this being a big step up, WATERFORD CASTLE should improve after making a promising start when 3rd to Saba Desert in a Maiden Stakes at Sandown 8 days ago. One to watch.

Debutant who shouldn't be totally ruled out for shrewd yard who are 2-6 with their turf 2yo's this season. Half brother to the US Grade 1 winner Sacred Wish and could go well at a price. Been nibbled at in the market and Holloway Boy won this as a first timer a few years ago.

Zooter is another debutant here and trainer Jack Jones is certainly not alone in holding the hopes in much higher regard than these odds suggest. Jones has a good record of overachieving with his 2 year olds on UK turf with a 9% win rate over the last 5 seasons with 5 winners from 56 runners, making Zooter well worth going in with here at these odds.

This horse has shown a decent level of form in France and now with willie Mullins he looks a cut above the opposition in this race. 
Has won recently over hurdles and can record a comfortable victory in this contest
Samui gets my vote over Sober who tends to run on ground with a bit more give than today and my pick could build on Tuesdays C2 third here if fully recovered from that run
Oisin Murphy states his best chance would be on Andrew Baldings Wild Waves and that will do for me if it stays?..he calls it a standout!!..player
Has won on 3 of 12 starts to date. Has never been over this far before but has ability and holds an eachvway chance

TROOPER BISDEE has at least an each-way squeak; after resuming to the track with an encouraging 5th to Manxman on return at Goodwood 4 weeks ago. He has won five times in nine runs (56%) on good-to-firm or similar going & has won six times in sixteen runs (38%) for trainer Sir Mark Prescott. One to watch.

Tashkan has been a useful stayer who has probably had a few issues that have puzzled his connections at times. He showed so much promise early on but hasn't quite converted it as many though he might. Irish raider Sober looks the one on paper but races aren't run on that stuff, so anything is possible. Very f ew of these appeal as betetr staying types than Tashkan but if he doesn't measure up in this average-looking lineup goes then I'd say it might be decision time for the connections around his future. For the odds.

The majority of the field will not stay that is not the case with Scottish Anthem. Poor run at Huntingdon where he was pulled up having gone off 15/8 favourite. At 66/1 is worth a bet gt placed with so many certain not to stay this trip

Despite having a lot to find on these terms, PARADOXICAL is now up significantly in trip after being well-held over 10 & 12 furlongs at Chester the last twice respectively. Jockey Warren Fentiman has placed six times in eight rides (75%) when aboard, winning four (50%) & Paradoxical has placed ten times in nineteen runs (53%) for trainer Jennie Candlish, winning six (32%). Lively outsider.

Satono Reve is a very speedy type who will take some beating.
Japanese horses tend to be underestimated in this country and it will take a good one to lower his colours here.

The 4yo was a smart 3L winner of a 14 runner Group 1 race at Royal Ascot last year, over this 6f trip on fast ground. Big return run when winning a Group 2 after 8 months off the track - high RPR rating - he doesn't meet that runner-up again but that pair had pulled a nice 4L clear of the rest. Should be better for the run and now has William Buick in the saddle for this Group 1.

Inisherin won this race last year and returns with a strong chance of repeating the feat, but I’m siding with Lazzat, who caught the eye last summer when storming to victory in the Group 1 Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville, pulling clear by an easy three lengths. Since then, he’s been tried over longer distances with respectable efforts, but this is a horse with natural speed, and his profile suggests that anything beyond seven furlongs may stretch him, so this stiff six furlongs looks ideal. Trainer Jerome Reynier dropped him back to sprinting last time out at Chantilly, and he looked right at home, winning comfortably in a quick time. Wathnan Racing wasted no time snapping him up with this target in mind, and he’s well drawn, close to where the early pace is expected. With further improvement likely, he could prove to be an unexposed Group 1 sprinter in the making and land the spoils at around 3/1.

Flora Of Bermuda was probably thought to need going on the soft side of good to show her best before her latest run at York on good to firm behind Inisherin beaten only a neck where she was waiting for room over a furlong out. Should go close here.
Impressive on return when winning over seven furlongs. Has strong form over shorter and this race could be run to suit. Strong player.

Elite Status has always looked a very good horse and he had a pipe opener for this when 4th behind Inisherin at York. He looked like he needed that and he can be in the mix for this race at a decent price.

Lightly Raced 4yo Sajir comes here with something to prove in this very competitive race drawn in stall 3 which is a positive in my opinion as in recent years the winner has come from stall 3 and this horse has the ability/potential to be right involved if breaking well and finding the right path which I'm confident Oisin Murphy will execute

A commendable performer who delivered his top performance of the season by placing 3rd out of 7 in a listed race at Salisbury 4 weeks ago. Trainer Mike Appleby often profits from runners that have cheekpieces applied for the first time. An each-way bet at 50/1 appears to be a promising opportunity for this this winner at this course and distance.

It’s all about the start for GRAND GREY, who blew it at the Curragh latest after shaping well when 2nd to Sajir in the Group 3 Abernant Stakes at Newmarket prior. Jockey Jamie Spencer has placed once in two rides (50%) when aboard & Grand Grey has placed four times in five runs (80%) on good-to-firm or similar going. Lively outsider.

GREAT GENERATION remains a progressive four year old filly who has possibly been set aside for this challenge on the back of her seasonal reappearance win last month. She now steps up considerably in class having scored three times in Group 3 company and not looking out of place in this line-up she could surprise.

I think this horse has bags of ability and given that ability, I do think he is a bit overpriced and looks to be versatile which is very useful on turf but serious step up in class, now going up 3 classes but not one to be underestimated.

Lightly raced 3yo. Two runs this year. Hampered in the Irish 2000 Guineas last time out. A narrow defeat on his return in a Group 3 against Group 1 class rivals. Top jockey Ryan Moore takes over in the saddle and he looks a standout at this Group 3 level.
Bumped into one when second in a Listed race at Newmarket last time. Still low mileage and would have a good chance with a repeat. Leading contender.

REMMOOZ should make his presence felt in this higher grade, after quickening clear in impressive style when beating Circios & 14 others in a Novice Stakes at Doncaster 2 weeks ago. Jockey Callum Rodriguez has won once in one ride (100%) when aboard & Remmooz has won twice in two runs (100%) over 7 furlongs. Every chance.
50/1 second in the Irish 1000 guineas and has to prove that was no fluke by running to form here. If she does it will put her well and truly in the mix.

This horse did remarkable well in the greenham stakes after a long absence on only his second start.
May well make up into a top group horse and winning this race today may prove to be just yhe first in a long line of top race wins.
Has so much potential and difficult to ignore at these odds.

The Gosdens horses have been firing on all cylinders this week at Royal Ascot and I am tipping Spy Chief can win for Godolphin in this Jersey Stakes. A winner the week before last at Yarmouth and my tip is Spy Chief is the boss in this Group 3.

Big price with 4 places on offer for a horse who finished just 4l behind Field Of Gold in The Craven Stakes and followed it up with a lesser run behind Ruling Court in the Guineas. Has enough class to be involved in this at a tasy looking 16/1
Brian returned from a break in April to a fourth here in a G3 just 2L away from the winner and I would expect more now second up EW 4P
Nobel Champion from the Ed Walker yard is back to what looks its best trip so at juicy odds it looks a player and the yard had q placed horse rhis week at big odds

Some of these just don’t look to have any sort of chance in a relatively weak affair. I had shortlisted 3 of the top 4 in the market, but another look at this and I think an outsider could sneak something, and the one I’ll chance is Seagulls Eleven. He was disappointing in the 2000gns on return, there’s no getting away from that, but the drop in trip is in his favour with his best form over 7, and he’s got a high draw so can hopefully keep out of trouble. He actually ran ok until he got completely unbalanced going into the dip and faded badly. I can forgive him that, and indeed he could be the one to blaze a trail here having done so previously, and with an overall lack of a front runner in the race if someone sets the right fractions up front they could sneak this. Harry Davies returns having been aboard for the horses only win, so that’s a plus to his chances. He’s vulnerable to something that has a bit of sparkle in the form line, but he looks too big to me regardless.

Lots of chances in this field and feel like many punters are swerving One Smack Mac based on bare form, but really it reads better than it looks. The winner of the last race has since won a group 3 in game fashion and likely front running here could be beneficial. Could each way chance.
Improved since swithed to sprinting distance for new yard. The strong pace will be in his favor and connections have done well in this race. Big shout.

Given his connections, there’s a strong sense that Jarraaf has been trained specifically for this race as his main seasonal target, especially considering his excellent course and distance record. He produced his best performances last year when dropped to this trip at Ascot, scoring two effortless wins and finishing a close second in Group 3 company. He returned last month with a single run at Salisbury, a very different type of track, where he pulled hard early on and understandably tired late. This race presents a completely different and more suitable test, and with that reappearance under his belt, he should strip much fitter. The draw isn’t ideal, but Billy Loughnane, who has already won on him here and rides the straight course well, is back in the saddle. So far, Loughnane has been partnering longshots throughout the meeting, but at 8/1, Jarraaf represents his best chance of grabbing a Royal Ascot winner. With bookies going 6 places, this looks a cracking each-way proposition, provided the draw doesn’t prove decisive.
Finally broke the hoodoo winning at Newbury after finishing four times on the bounce - once by a head and twice by a short head. Has won a few times prior, and retains top jockey on board
Purosangue is trained by Andrew Balding (21 per cent strike rate in last fornight , including 2 RA handicaps) and is the mount of the in form Oisin Murphy.Well drawn in 22.Each way chance.

Holkham Bay's Ascot record reads 2-1-1, with the most recent win coming from a mark of 95 - just 2lbs lower than today. We saw on Friday that the pace bias flipped and he is drawn on the high side but with Valiant Force in the stall next door he should get a good pace to aim at, and showed LTO that he's running back into form after his winter break.

The curtain closing wild sprint, and it’s a minefield, but I was willing to chance class to out in this handicap with Zoum Zoum looking a fairly big price. She’s reappeared with a decent Listed 2nd suggesting all ground is alike to her, she was a solid 5th in the Jersey last year when seemingly taking to this track. She’s run well on seasonal reappearance and around race fit horses, so I think you can mark up a career best RPR last time as a result.

This horse won this race in 2023 and looks to have been campaigned to arrive here on an attractive mark to win it again. The booking of Colin Keane certainly catches the eye and this is a really classy horse having gone down by less than half a length in a French Group 1 before which shows he has the ability to win this ultra competitive race again

High class sprinter who has done all his winning at Newmarket but was a very solid 4th off this mark in the Palace of Holyrood House last year. Two starts at HQ this spring should have put him spot on for this and so should run very well.

A 4 times career winner who won the Group 2 Norfolk Stakes here back in 2023 and went on to finish second to Bg Evs in the Breeders Cup Grade 1 Juvenile Turf Sprint later that year. Has won 3 times since them including twice at Dundalk earlier in the year. Not so good the last twice but they were over longer trips with the last time on unsuitable soft ground so they can be forgiven. This is probably the target and has the ability to go close.

One of my favourite races of the entire season here, however finding the winner looks as tough as always. If you look at Korker's third at Hamilton last time he has absolutely no chance in this. However all his best form has come in these big field handicaps, primarily his third in the Ayr Gold Cup last year. He ran a promising race in York sprint handicap ay York's Dante meeting, confirming he retains all his ability. I'm still of the view that high numbers have an advantage on the straight course, and from box 24 Korker can, hopefully, run a corker.

Shartash has raced soley on the AW this year and all 4 of his turf wins have been in small fields but this gelding has raced mostly at Group level on turf and this time last year, he was only beaten around 5 lengths in the Group 1 6f Jubilee Stakes.
Down in the weights, suited by the quick ground and first time cheekpieces, could see a big run today.

GERMANIC is not without prospects, who may do better still after getting back on the up when 2nd to Ferrous at Newcastle 6 weeks ago. He has placed twice in five runs (40%) within this sphere (class 2) & has placed once in two runs (50%) for trainer Miss Julie Camacho. One to watch.

Made all when winning in impressive style over a furlong further at Newmarket on penultimate start but disappointed over that same trip here last month when 16th of 17. Reportedly upset in the stalls in that latest race and the first time tongue-tie could help with the drop in trip of appeal too.

Won the Norfolk stakes in 2023 as a 150/1 shot and although the career hasn't really panned out after that run a return to Ascot and firm ground conditions may bring out plenty of improvement and he can out run his odds.

Is 8lb lower than when a close third in this race three years ago and though has also flopped at another couple of Ascot meetings was mixing it in Group 1 company. Has run well this season including when a close fourth to subsequent Kensington Palace winner Miss Information giving that smart filly loads of weight. Ran well enough again last time in the Victoria Cup here over 7f and drop to a stiff 6f can help him run well in this. Yard already had a top sprint winner this week in Havana Hurricane and hopefully that one had given my speculative poke here some advice! Could go well at a price and another EW poke in this ultra competetive race.

Unbeaten in four on good to firm and has only had three runs since winning the Jersey Stakes for Charlie Appleby at this meeting three years ago. 3 tame efforts in those three years since hardly inspire confidence but back at the scene of his big win might be a sneaky one to keep an eye on. Conditions suit and hopefully we've landed on a plan for another new yard.

Has only had 4 career starts to date with 1 win at Lingfield on good to firm in class 5 maiden over 7f & then 2 placed efforts on soft at Redcar in class 4 & then an encouraging run after 202 day break when finishing 2nd at Sandown on good in class 2 over 8f 57 days ago beaten 0.75L by Fifth Column but staying on well at the business end so today's extra 2f should suit , yard a bit quiet so far at meeting a bit of a worry .
Impressive when winning last time from last to first. Still look ahead of the handicaper and this could be a Group horse in the making. The one to beat.

The stable is in good form so SALLAAL must be noted, who is open to improvement after beating Arctic Grey & 3 others in a Novice Stakes at Hamilton 7 weeks ago. Jockey Ray Dawson has won once in one ride (100%) when aboard & Sallaal has also won once in one run (100%) on good-to-firm or similar going. One to watch.

In the each-way market, the list of contenders is long, with several making appeal to get involved. I’ll leave the London Gold Cup form behind, despite suspecting it's quite strong, and instead side with El Burhan, a horse who has been given plenty of time to mature by George Boughey, who won this race in 2022 with Missed The Cut and hasn’t had a runner in the last two renewals. That suggests he feels he has a realistic chance with this interesting type. A dual-winner at Yarmouth and Beverley last season, El Burhan signed off his juvenile campaign with an excellent third in a valuable big-field nursery at Goodwood, before being put away for the winter. He returned with an immediate success this season over 7½ furlongs at Chester, keeping on steadily without being flashy. His pedigree and racing style suggest he needs time to warm up, and he should be an even better proposition over today’s longer trip. He’s been raised only 2lb for that Chester win, so there’s every reason to believe he remains well-handicapped, especially if he improves again for the step up in distance. At 12/1,he’s a solid each-way bet, particularly with bookies paying 5/6 places.

4th in the London Gold Cup over this trip at Newbury last time out, keeping on well and only beaten 1.75 lengths ridden by William Buick who retains the ride. Originally declared for this and the King George V Handicap over a mile and a half yesterday. Connections obviously feel this shorter trip will suit more and the first time cheekpieces offer potential improvement.

Tycoon has only had three runs but returned from a break in April to a C5 win on GF and was not bad when second up in listed company and third at 1m3f and I think the return to 1m2f and dropping to C2 could work with cheekpieces today
Form is very much hit or miss and O'Brien hasn't worked out his ideal trip yet. Battled on bravely when winning at Leopardstown and they could use these positive tactics again.

Kept good company as a 2yo and was unlucky not win maiden on third start when beaten a head at Dundalk. Had earlier run well against two Aidan O'Brien hotpots including the very talented Lion In Winter who could still make up into a good one. Was a very easy winner on 3yo debut at the stiff Navan improving for the step up in trip and was unlucky not to follow up when nutted a short head in an ultra competitive handicap back at the same track. Improving and has got a good draw hopefully and can go well at a price in an open race now that right trip has been found.,

Back to back wins at Ballinrobe and Fairyhouse last month and I am backing Fantazy Man won’t be too far away in this Golden Gates Stakes. The cheekpieces have really helped this three year and I am going for Seamie Heffernan delivering for Murtagh in the Golden Gates.

aurel won his last race well and he beat a horse rated 94 so off that mark today on his handicap debut and with further improvement he should be right in the mix.he looks like he will see out the trip better than most and at 18/1 looks great value

Brindavan returned from a break in March after being gelded to three runs so far, opening with a C4 second then stepped up to C3 off an 84 an was pants but did improve when third up off the same mark with a C3 win and could continue his improvement as is up 6 lbs for that but that still puts him well light among today's C2 runners EW 5P
Finished 7l behind future Guineas winner Ruling Court at Meydan back in March and a winner since then. Could be more to come and at a big price.

Price is too big. There are questionable marks about many of these and most have a bit to prove. AOB has obviously rated this horse highly enough to contend at the top level both last year and this. He hasn't made it, but there could still be potential there to win at this level and above. 6l behind French Guineas winner Henri Matise in March and 7l behind one of the Epsom Derby favourites Delacroix after that. This should be a lot easier.

BASALT now sports the cheekpieces for the first-time on handicap bow, with the slightly shorter trip likely to suit after making a creditable reappearance when 5th to Amiloc in the Listed Cocked Hat Stakes at Goodwood 4 weeks ago. He has won once in four runs (25%) for trainer Archie Watson. Lively outsider.
Was a winner at uttoxeter on penultimate start but took a tumble at Worcester last time. Has every chance if recovering from that experience

The model I run suggests Cap Du Nord can win this one. This model result has been dirven by Cap Du Nord having the highest RPR by quite some amount over the other 4 runners in this 5 horse race. Cap Du Nord lines up here with the second lowest official ranking, which subsequently means going out with the second lowest weight to carry on this longer 3m trip. Last ran 29 days ago so race fitness shouldn't be a concern but needs to go better than that to get over the line first. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Great d'Ange came back last year from an unsuccessful spell in point to points to win a three mile two furlong handicap chase at Newton Abbot at 80-1 off a mark of 100 he has not won since and came back over two miles five furlongs at Stratford but tired quickly two out after leading that was his first run for 234 days and he should strip fitter.

Having been placed in his previous four races this D McCain jnr trained 7-y-o gelding won for the first in his latest start over this course and distance on good ground 15 days ago when beating the P Griffin trained Herja by 2 3/4 lengths so with B S Hughes in the saddle he can follow up today

The model I run suggests And She Was can win this one. And She Was lines up here with a comarably high RPR but has by far the lowest weight to carry around this 2m trip. Only 4 years old so the youngest runner going out here and loosk for some improvement to make an impression. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Barranco can win this one. This model result has been driven by Barranco having the highest RPR of the 4 runner field an has an official ranking that leaves him very well treated off this mark. Goes out around this 2m 1f trip with 10 lbs less than current market competitor tactical affair and 1 stone 10 lbs to the top weight. Barranco has great form figures and comes here with 2 back to back wins, the last one being 29 days ago so race fitness is not a concern. Prior course and distance winner and looks to repeat. Model has issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.75pt take on a scale of 0-4.

Collingham has switched stables again to Jake Coulson after winning another claiming hurdle, he has only run once over fences when 3rd of 5 beaten just over three lengths at Ffos Las in April and Tabitha Worsley takes off three pounds. His current mark of 117 gives him a good chance of his first chase win against three opponents considering bottom weight Barranco has rocketed up eighteen pounds since his latest easy win.

James Owen stable in fantastic form recently and they have a good chance of adding to their winning strike rate of 20% with Chillhi. Form of Cartmel race boosted with Winds of Winter going on to win again in impressive fashion - 4th that day has also went to win against a clear cut subsequent winner. Ticks alot of boxes here. NAP

Spartan Warrior won consecutive handicaps on the flat in May 2024 and finally got off the mark over hurdles at Kelso last time grinding out a win taking it up on the runin and only up two pounds he could follow up at Bangor.

Land Girls Luck won last time after the progressive leader (who won next time) fell at the last. Was clear of the rest at the time. Saddle slipped and PU on penultimate start when going well. Previous two runs were also good efforts (while still learning) and the form has been well franked. Today's trip looks ideal, and the 6-year-old with rider's claim is on a good mark and gets the ground well. Good value to follow up with another win.

The model I run suggests Karakoy can cause an upset here and win this one. Karakoy lines up here with the joint highest RPR of this 7 runner race but has an official ranking that leaves Karakoy very well treated off this mark. Goes out carrying the lowest weight by a wide margin around this 2m 3f trip. Tries the visor for the first time to aid concentration and if the headgear works there should be some improvement in form. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Lord Cauvelliere won a point bumper at Bitterley in April being held up to beat Eddie My Eagle, he then won very comfortably against the same horse in a bumper at Stratford despite running more prominently and the 2nd being held up. He could win again giving a stone to mare Flying Pimpernel who was 2nd at Fontwell.

Disappointed on both of first 2 starts. Last seen in April and makes first start for new yard today. Should be better than those performances have shown and any improvement will give an each way chance

the model I run suggests Special Dragon can win this one. Special Dragon lines up here with the second lowest RPR but has the lowest official ranking. This subsequently means Special Dragon steps out carrying the lowest weight over this 2m 4f trip. Special dragon comes here with some form being shown , with figures of 53-25. Needs to improve on that to go first here. Prior distance winner so knows how to get it done at this trip. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Twice a hurdles winner who finished 4th on chasing debut before winning at ffos las on 2nd start over fences. Should be there or thereabouts

Sits just 3lbs above her last winning mark. Returning to the scene of her most recent win. 
She won her only run over CD around this time last year. With Sean Bowen booked. She won with plenty in hand. Beating the Dan Skelton trainer Gentle Connections a little over 5L. A comfortable success. 
She struggled for the next few runs. The fact the handicapper raised her 10lbs for that CD win gave her little hope off a career high mark. 
Her 2nd run after her break off a 1lb higher mark than this caught the eye. She stayed on nicely enough to grab 2nd place behind Irish Lullaby. She pulled 20L clear of the 3rd horse Annie Nail. 
She put in a lesser run lto. She didn't jump very well. I'm putting that down to Warwick being an unsuitable track (0/4 there). If she can repeat the penultimate run. She should go well in this type of race.

Lost Connections went off too fast over three miles on her first run for Jake Coulson and her stamina gave out well before the end on her first run for 234 days, she will be better suited to two and a half miles and Tabitha Worsley takes over the ride from Sean Bowen.

Bellbird has only won once from fourteen attempts over hurdles but she has finished 2nd five times since that win under Brian Hughes at Ludlow in May 2024 and despite the handicapper pushing her up a pound for each of her latest two 2nd places she is overdue another win for Brian Hughes.

The form of his Doncaster triumph in March is bombproof and just didn't for the first time fire at Huntingdon after that. His latest sixth in a competitive handicap hurdle at Aintree was more like it and you can pick holes in the rest of these. McCain-trained horses just seem to improve about 10lb at Bangor and I'm hopeful of a big performance.
Mo of Cairo's chances here stick out like a sore thumb and given the way the last race has worked out, will take some pegging back here.

Woohoo rattled of a quickfire hat-trick before finishing second at Hamilton earlier in the week. The horse that beat him there was running up his own three timer and is absolutely flying just now. The opposition in this modest looking heat isn't great, and Woohoo looks by far the most likely winner.
Ayr punt today in 8.08 two time course and distance winner over this trip. Got to have a squeak at this level topof my punting list on Saturday
Good second behind an experienced handicapper in Faylaq, it feels like Creatif remains open to progress and looks a good bet here.
Stayed on inside the final furlong over the extended mile and a half at York 8 days ago and will welcome the step up in trip being a winner over this trip and over further,

Irish raider who has skipped 2 meetings in Ireland for this contest. Looked good in all weather events at Dundalk before being given tough tasks in listed events on turf. This is calmer waters and could run into a place at double figure odds

Withdrawn recently from a similar Hamilton handicap.
Intriguing they did that and reappear here so soon afterwards with Jason hart on board.
Big chance today if reproducing his beat form so at the current odds looks good value.
A horse that is proven in pattern class and who truly looks the class angle in here. Top course jockey booking and no reason why this horse can't capitalise here.
Excellent third last time to Symbol Of Hope , Jockey and trainor in top form , will be there at the business end of the race .

GRANDE MARQUES already has black-type , so the feeling is Irish connections will be looking to land a few bets in this Listed-class race. A largely progressive filly with a notable Australian sprint sire and with half an eye on the market she could be the answer.
Rosy affair has been very well backed here in this listed race, seems a big price considering the horse ran well after eight months off at Newmarket

SARATOGA SPECIAL is an interesting three year old filly representing a powerful Irish yard. Trainer Jess Harrington's string have turned a corner in recent weeks amd although something to find on official ratings that would not be a huge issue.

Tristian Davidson is 4 wins from his last 8 runs and has a great chance of adding to that strike rate with Coconut Bay. Has hit the frame on all 4 runs at Ayr and is in good form with that form working out well. Jason Hart takes the reigns and hes operating at a 22% win strike rate. Should go well. NB

Won under the stable jockey last time out, running very green, had to switch multiple times to get a clear run-in, then kept hanging under pressure. Did very well to win that day and is up 5lbs. Jockey claiming 7lbs. Yard also has the stable jockey on Water of Leith who is more fancied that Classy Al, but with our horse liking the hold up run, I think he can pick up at the run-in. A lot would've been learn by the horse last time out.

Winner of this race last year who hasn't shown a great deal in just 4 starts since but has slipped to 2ob below last year's winning mark so is worth a speculative investment this afternoon on that basis.

Had a shocker LTO at Chester when 11 of 11 last month but I think going LTO not to his advantage and softer ground expected tomorrow should make life a bit easier and just 1lb higher than last winning mark and drop down in class should help.

This Ollie Sangster trained filly can make it third time lucky after being placed in her first two races the latest over six furlongs on good to firm ground at Redcar when only beaten a neck in second of the 12 runners behind the well backed T D Easterby trained Bleep Test and with J P Spencer booked it looks like a win today
Blooming Legend 2 year old with Charlie clover. Ran ok on debut, finishing 5th. Take a chance she could overturn the short price favourite here.

This D O'Meara trained 3-y-o filly improved from her racecourse debut to only be beaten a neck behind the Miss J A Camacho trained Patricia R over seven furlong on good to soft ground at Thirsk so on a sounder surface and Jason Watson doiung the steering she looks hard to oppose
Disappointed on debut in June last year when only 8th of 11. Should be better than that and yard has been in good form. Holds an each way chance if finding some improvement
Richerd Hannon horse not reall taken to the all weather had break since last seen and now back on turf worth a big consideration

Skimming Along won at long odds last time and has barely been punished going into a handicap today. Striking quickly for a double would be quite impressive given this one started 400 250 and 300 in first three races.
Disappointed on 3 starts on the all weather but did have wide draws to contend with. Improved on turf debut to win at Yarmouth 10 days ago. Should be there or thereabouts
Similar thing happened last time with this horse here when dropped back into 0-50 company, and always dropping back down to 7f this for me is the horse to beat.
Mainly races on the all weather and has placed in 2 of ladt 5 outings. Holds an each way chance if bringing that form to this surface

Rusheen Boy smashed the rivals to bits in a similar contest 9 days ago, despite a 12lb hammering from the accesor, the gelding can back that victory up here with the jockey taking off a handy 7lb. The selection effectively runs off a mark of 53 tonight taking into account the jockeys claim. He looks one to keep on the right side off currently. Having previously won off a mark of 65, he can continue to take advantage the reduced turf rating. The only slight negative is the inexperienced jockeys record (just 1 career win, for this yard) but she is the yards apprentice so probably knows the horse having ridden out. Hopefully this spinter shouldn't take much steering for the young jockey over the straight 6f at Lingfield.
Unfortunately not coming here in the best of form but now only 2lbs higher than last winning mark and ideally some rain tomorrow would be useful but I still think he can be competitive.

Most firms have gone odds on but B365 are evens for GOLD DAWN and I can’t escape that price. B Garritty does awfully on Saturdays (8% SR, A/E 0.43) which makes Penhallam hard to side with, meanwhile Soldier’s Call’s 6% SR (A/E 0.45) with runners in June suggests that Eyes Front won’t come forward from his two starts to date. It’s difficult to make a case for the double-digit runners so GD could just win by default as well as on merit; the colt by Havana Gold was a 1.25l 2nd of 8 on debut over C&D last month, looking like making all a furlong out before taking a bad step and being eased. He’s surely capable of building on that from a yard who are overperforming of late (14% SR, A/E 1.56 over the past month) with a top booking in J Mitchell.
Is well bred and showed plenty of promise when finishing 4th on debut. Improved on that to finish 2nd last time and that form sets a standard in this. Looks like the one to beat
Performed admirably at Lingfield last time and gave the front two a run for their money despite spurning the golden highway up the rail that day. Good chance to go better here

Amestris 3 year old bay filly out of Mehmas. Highly tried as a 2 year old last season, made her comeback this season in a competitive race at York were she tied significantly late on, which was not surprising as this was her first run for sometime. Gone down 2 pound in the handicap she should run better today.
Not seen since a disappointing effort in february but has won 2 of last 4 races. Needs to bounce back after this break but holds an each way chance if finding best form

Course and distance winner who has found himself an excellent opportunity to get back on the winning boards was last seen at Chelmsford 20 days ago where finishing 8th/15 and shaped much better than that bare result suggest a good analysis of this class 4 handicap clearly shows Helm Rock will be well suited in a assignment of this nature with an ideal pace level likely to be set given the horses enrolled to run here currently operating on an extremely dangerous mark of 79 D & C Kubler's inmate looks poised to strike here and worth noting he is now operating 4lb below his last winning mark jockey J Mitchell takes the ride and can give Helm Rock a promising ride here at Haydock expect to see this strongly built individual thundering home and playing a huge role in this Class 4 handicap over on the business end
At a price, Eagle Day looks an interesting each way play here. Nothing to shout about this term, but won this last year. Hoping for a strong showing

Winner at Windsor in August. Remained in good form for the rest of the season and took a step forward from reappearance when 2nd at Goodwood a fortnight ago. Should run very well once again this evening.

INTO BATTLE was something of an eye catcher last time out and a reletively quick turnaround often reads well. He has a good draw for early track position taking in this left-hand turn and apparently with nothing to hold him back racing from this career-low handicap mark he appeals.

Should have won the last day, Joe Fanning managed to get him boxed in on the rail. Should go very close today might be worth backing EW but I'm going for the win to make up for the last day. Form are flying too.
Backed into 15-2 from 14-1 at Chester last time out but lost all chance when blowing the start. Eased in grade to Class 4 from Class 2 and worth another look over this longer trip.
Has been in good form since entering handicap company and has won all of last 4 races. Up another 7lb but likely to be there or thereabouts again

The U.S. Navy Flag filly demonstrated her potential in her initial 2 outings, and with a visor added, she triumphed in an 8 runner maiden at this venue just 22 days ago, finishing strong to take the lead. Its probable that she will improve further now that she's entering the handicap ranks, making her a strong contender.
Trainer does well in this race and Sound of Lightning remains a pretty unexposed type. Every chance here in a warm race

Alfred Tennyson may edge this if the blinkers going on bring any kind of significant benefit. This looks like a coinflip against Knockmark who was second last time. Aidan O Brien coming off the back of a good week and Ascot can get another here.
Twice raced 3yo, placed at Dundalk last time out at 8f, down in trip today should suit, in form 5lb claimer takes over, yard in form, must have a good chance

Acapulco Bay has run in Group and Listed races but seems not quite up to that class but handicaps looks as if they will be a better prospect in his career. Bred very blue blooded and May in future progress to Graded Level. He is only a three year old so has time.
This Premier Handicap presents an easier task to the horse as his class will come to the top of the pack and this may be his day. The distance seems good and the trip should be fine given breeding. Fancied by many, me included.
Yet to win from 3 starts but has shown plenty of promise placing in 2 of those 3 races. On a competitive mark for handicap debut and should be there or thereabouts
Slowly progressive type for a yard that isn't adverse to landing a touch, wouldn't be surprised if this horse went off shorter and certainly would want to follow it in.

Yet to run a bad race and despite disappointing when beaten favourite on last run, had the excuse of returning from a break and should strip fitter now. Form behind Lake Victoria majorly boosted with that horse 6 wins from 7 and finishing ahead of Cicirene who won a valuable race at Ascot yesterday. This is calmer waters and looks worthy favourite
Dropping back down to this seemingly preferred trip, the chances of Diamond Exchange really jump off the page here in a field full of questions

A lightly-raced winner who recently secured an impressive 2nd out of 8 in a handicap at Fairyhouse 23 days ago. Has a solid chance on form. Nicola burns will be in the saddle and has placed twice at Limerick from 3 starts.

WAIT FOR IT has at least as much scope as any of these three year olds and she is of interest on her handicap debut with this yard among the recent winners. They also punt runners expected to oblige , so with the market in mind this filly from a workable looking opening mark appeals.

COLUGO does have to bounce back from a disappointing effort on her recent handicap debut. She steps up in trip here hooded also and her mark would not appear to be any barrier to success. She has in general looked better this year and given her draw may force her hand she could surprise.

Has only won once from 19 starts but has finished 2nd on 4 occasions. Had not been since November when finishing 8th of 18 at leopardstown 2 weeks ago. Probably needed that run and holds every chance if rediscovering best form.

Cala Bonita has taken well to life in handicaps from first 2 runs: 2nd on debut and went one better next time out to win with a bit in hand over Clever and Classy - that horse has since run a cracker when maybe doing too much too soon and being caught by a well backed rival yesterday at this venue. The first 4 were clear a long way of the remaning 13 runners. This horse still races off a low weight and should follow up with a bold show here
Has shown some promise in 3 starts to date. Drop in trip likely to suit for handicap debut and has an each way chance if finding some improvement

YES OUI SI presumably has a distinct amount of ability due to the weight of support she has recieved on her last two starts. The ground may have been against her last time , so assuming the money comes again then she could prove decent odds from the overnight market.
Cromwell horse up seven pound for recent win and this distance suits might take a lot of beating in attempt to follow up here

STEPS IN THE SAND is a mare who may have turned a corner on the evidence of her most recent flat handicap. She did begin to thrive at around this early summer time last year and with Shane Foley booked there are reasons to be hopeful for a big run.

APPLEJACK POET has a wider than ideal draw to overcome , but a mile and a half imn which to do so and he could be well treated switching codes. He is race-sharp from three recent runs under the NH code and appeals as a value player.

Junkyard Dog won at Navan in April and has gone well at Cork and Leopardstown of a 8lbs higher mark since. He is dropped 3lbs here and with his useful Claimer taking of another 7lbs he looks to have a great chance of going in again

Ronan Whelan is in fine form and can continue that with this course winner. Barrogstown Girl won over 1m3f here last year on good ground. Has progressed well after returning from a break, took a big step forward on last run when only beaten 2 lengths. Decent strike rate with 3 wins from 12 runs, still unexposed and should run a good race getting weight from majority of the field

GOD OF THUNDER has been freshened up since a spell hurdling and this smart dual-purpose Irish yard are in much better form now which can see this experienced six year old to good effect. He has dropped to an attractive mark for a flat handicap , so he seems a likely type.
Has been improving steadily and won comfortably over course and distance last time out. Can go in again now returning to handicaps.

Deuteronomy may well be in the handicappers grasp - up 14lb since winning last 2 runs but has looked like theres another big run in there and the form of last few runs has worked out well. Can't write off for hat trick bid

EXCEEDING was a huge gamble last time out and second-up for this spell this four year old will be straighter. His 10lb presumably stable apprentice will also know more about him having been aboard that day and he could be one of the more likely types at decent odds.
May not get a run as only 3rd reserve but has won 3 times over this distance and has been showing signs of returning to form. Each way chance if making the field

I've backed CHOU CHOU, Eamonn O'Connell's four-year-old gelding, a few times now - although he didn’t get in from 3rd reserve the last time I tried. I thought he ran well at Gowran Park at the beginning of April, finishing just three lengths off the winner. Cork looked a bit too sharp for him on his penultimate start, and last time out here at Limerick, I don't think he disgraced himself over what now looks, in hindsight, to have been a trip too short (7f).
This son of BELARDO drops another 3lb in the handicap and now gets the assistance of promising 5lb claimer Wayne Hassett, which should help his cause. It's no surprise to see trainer Eamonn O'Connell boasting a 30.77% place strike rate at Limerick - a track where his runners tend to go well. Connections reach for the cheekpieces today, adding them to the tongue tie already in use, which could help sharpen this lad up.
I definitely think there’s a race in CHOU CHOU somewhere, and whether that’s today remains to be seen. But at current odds of 20/1, I’m happy to nail my colours to the mast and go each-way.
Has contested an assortment of races at different grades/trips and grounds, won on debut last Sept and 5 runs since , 2/10 last time out in G3 with first go at 12f, in form jockey/trainer combo

An effective gelding. He has won at this C&D. With odds of 33/1, he finished in 4th place in a listed race at Leopardstown 16 days ago, having missed the break. Now with a significant increase in trip and cheekpieces back on, it's a tough challenge, but he is certainly capable of rising to it.
